highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: Friday's security updates cover dozens of packages across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Slackware, and SUSE, including kernel, OpenSSL, and PostgreSQL.
highlights.detail: Updates address recent CVEs in the listed packages, improving system security. Administrators should apply them promptly to mitigate potential exploits. The breadth of affected distributions highlights coordinated effort across Linux ecosystems.

highlights.title: Git-bug: Distributed, offline-first bug tracker embedded in Git
highlights.summary: Git-bug is a distributed, offline‑first bug tracker that lives inside Git repositories.
highlights.detail: Git‑bug stores bug reports as Git objects, enabling versioned history and offline collaboration. It works without a central server, syncing through standard Git pushes and pulls. The tool is licensed under MIT.

highlights.title: Hackaday Podcast Episode 388: RAM-Swapping on Raspberry Pi, Raindrops on Radar, and a Fine Mesh
highlights.summary: Hackaday Podcast Episode 388 covers RAM‑swapping on Raspberry Pi, raindrop detection radar, and fine‑mesh networking, plus hacker advice.
highlights.detail: Episode 388 features a deep dive into RAM‑swapping techniques that extend Raspberry Pi memory, a radar project detecting raindrops for atmospheric studies, and a discussion on fine‑mesh network design. Hosts also share mentorship advice for emerging hackers.

highlights.title: Proaction boosts sales 60% and saves 75+ hours with Codex
highlights.summary: Proaction reports a 60% sales increase and over 75 saved hours by using Codex, GPT‑Live‑1, and GPT‑6 Astra for fleet‑management development.
highlights.detail: Codex, GPT‑Live‑1, and GPT‑6 Astra are OpenAI models that generate code and automate deployment pipelines. Proaction integrated them into its fleet‑management platform, reducing manual coding effort. The time savings allowed engineers to focus on feature development, contributing to the sales lift.

highlights.title: google/langextract
highlights.summary: google/langextract is a Python library that extracts structured data from unstructured text using LLMs with source grounding and interactive visualization.
highlights.detail: langextract leverages large language models to parse free‑form text and output JSON or CSV structures, preserving citations to the original passages. Interactive visualizations help users explore extraction results. The library is compatible with popular LLM APIs.

items.title: Model: Edge0/Audio8-ASR-Infinite
items.summary: Edge0/Audio8-ASR-Infinite is an automatic speech recognition model with 2,853 downloads and 675 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is part of Edge0's suite for low‑latency speech recognition on embedded devices. Its popularity on Hugging Face reflects community interest in open‑source ASR solutions. Likes indicate positive reception among developers.

items.title: Model: abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-GGUF
items.summary: abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-GGUF is a text‑to‑image model with 715,906 downloads and 1,841 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: Qwen‑Image‑2.1‑Uncensored‑GGUF provides uncensored image generation in the efficient GGUF format, facilitating deployment on limited hardware. Its high download count shows strong demand for open‑source text‑to‑image tools. The repository includes conversion scripts.

items.title: A summary from the 2026 Git Contributors' Summit
items.summary: The 2026 Git Contributors' Summit summary notes discussions on Git 3.0, security processes, documentation, pluggable object database, and LLM integration.
items.detail: The summit previewed Git 3.0's planned features, such as improved performance and new plumbing commands. Security process enhancements aim to streamline vulnerability handling. Integration of LLMs into Git tooling was a notable topic.

items.title: Two stable kernels for Friday
items.summary: Linux stable kernels 7.2.8 and 6.18.54 were released, each containing multiple fixes.
items.detail: Kernel 7.2.8 belongs to the 7.x long‑term series, while 6.18.54 continues the 6.18 stable branch. Both releases incorporate bug fixes, driver updates, and security patches. Users of affected hardware are encouraged to upgrade.

items.title: Abusing SQL to Play DOOM
items.summary: Hackaday article shows how SQL can be abused to implement a playable DOOM engine.
items.detail: The article demonstrates constructing a DOOM game engine entirely in SQL, leveraging recursive queries and stored procedures. It showcases SQL's Turing‑complete capabilities beyond traditional data management. Code snippets are provided for replication.

items.title: Alban1911/Rose
items.summary: Alban1911/Rose is a Python project titled 'League, unlocked'.
items.detail: Rose appears to be a Python project related to unlocking features in a league‑style system, possibly a game or competition platform. The repository includes minimal documentation and a setup script.

items.title: AlexandreRouma/SDRPlusPlus
items.summary: AlexandreRouma/SDRPlusPlus is a cross‑platform software‑defined radio application written in C++.
items.detail: SDRPlusPlus supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, offering a modular architecture for signal processing, device control, and spectrum analysis. Written in modern C++, it integrates with popular SDR hardware like RTL‑SDR and Airspy.

items.title: CodeZeno/Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor
items.summary: A free, open‑source Windows taskbar widget that monitors usage limits and reset times for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other AI assistants.
items.detail: The widget resides in the Windows taskbar and provides a real‑time visual indicator of remaining quota. It can be configured with API keys for each service and supports multiple models, helping developers stay within usage caps.

items.title: akitaonrails/ai-usagebar
items.summary: A Rust‑implemented Waybar widget that displays current plan usage and remaining credits for Claude, GPT, GLM, and OpenRouter services.
items.detail: Designed for Linux desktop panels using Waybar, the widget reads credit information via each service's API. Inspired by claudebar/codexbar, it offers customizable appearance and alerts, reducing the risk of unexpected quota exhaustion.

items.title: androoAGI/starnet
items.summary: A local‑first desktop application that presents a pixel‑art station where user‑provided AI agents execute tasks using your own API keys.
items.detail: The app runs entirely on the user's machine, visualizing agents as pixel characters that perform real work. It supports bringing any compatible API key, enabling experimentation with autonomous AI crews without cloud dependencies.
